- Attempting to rewrite HEAD with commands like `git reset HEAD~N`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout <branch>`, or `git rebase` on the shared checkout → Use `git revert <sha>` to undo a published commit as a new commit, `git restore <path>` to restore a file to HEAD, or `git switch main` to move to a branch (never to rewrite HEAD) — The shared checkout feeds `src/core/` to all consumer projects via live symlinks, so rewriting HEAD breaks linear history and orphans work in sibling sessions _(seen 27×)_
